name: Crime Scene and Trauma Cleanup
h1: Crime Scene and Trauma Cleanup in Rockville and Montgomery County

meta.title: Crime Scene Cleanup Rockville MD | Black Ops
meta.description: Crime scene and trauma cleanup in Rockville and Montgomery County. Answered 24 hours, unmarked vehicles, and we speak to your insurer for you.

banner.subhead: When the investigators leave, the property is handed back. We take it from there, quietly, and we deal with your insurer. We answer at any hour, our vehicles carry no signage, and we are usually on site within two hours of the scene being released.

problem.heading: The part nobody tells you about
problem.lead: Police and the medical examiner secure a scene, gather what they need, and then release the property. Cleaning it is not their job and never has been.

voices.quote: Do the police not clean this up?
voices.source: Recurring enquiry, the most common surprise

voices.quote: Will the neighbours know what happened?
voices.source: Recurring enquiry, to be replaced with tracked call phrasing

voices.quote: I am the executor and I live out of state.

includes.heading: What the work covers
includes.note: We can also arrange for personal effects to be recovered, cleaned where possible, and returned to you rather than disposed of. Ask us at the assessment. People often only think of it later.

items.title: Containment
items.body: Put in place before anything is touched, so nothing spreads through the rest of the property.

items.title: Removal of affected material
items.body: Flooring, subfloor, drywall, furnishings. Blood travels into porous material further than it looks, which is why scrubbing a surface is not remediation.

items.title: Decontamination
items.body: Every affected surface, to hospital grade.

items.title: Fingerprint powder, chemical residue and evidence markers
items.body: Investigators leave these behind and most people do not expect it. It is part of the job, not an extra.

items.title: Odour treatment at source
items.body: Treated at the source rather than masked.

items.title: Regulated waste disposal
items.body: Through a licensed medical waste stream, with the manifest handed to you.

items.title: Written clearance
items.body: Confirming the property is safe for occupancy.

process.heading: What happens, and how long each part takes
process.note: Step two is specific to this page and it is genuinely useful. Families frequently call before the scene is released and nobody has told them that is why nothing can start.

steps.title: Confirming the scene is released

disclaimer.heading: One thing we will not do
disclaimer.body: We do not display CDC, EPA or OSHA seals to imply those agencies endorse us. They do not endorse anyone. We follow CDC and EPA disinfection guidance and our technicians are trained to the OSHA bloodborne pathogen standard. Those are facts, and they are worth more than a logo. If another company shows you federal seals, ask them what they mean.

pricing.heading: What this costs, and how you find out
pricing.note: We do not publish prices for this work. Scope varies too widely for a range to be useful, and quoting blind would be guessing. We assess at no charge and give you a written price before any work starts, and we tell you at that visit what your insurer is likely to cover.
pricing.footnote: You will never get a number from us that changes once the job is underway, unless we find something behind a wall that nobody could have seen. If that happens we stop, show you, and re-quote before continuing.

items.q: Do the police clean this up?
items.a: No. Investigators secure the scene, gather evidence and then release the property. Cleanup is the property owner's responsibility. Nobody tells you that in advance, and it is the single most common surprise for the people who call us.
Once investigators have released the scene. If you are not sure whether that has happened, tell us and we will find out for you.

items.q: Will anyone know what happened here?
items.a: Not from us. Our vehicles carry no signage, our technicians arrive in plain clothing and change on site, and we do not discuss jobs with neighbours or anyone else.

Usually yes, because it is sudden damage to the property. Some policies exclude suicide unless a rider was bought. Call your adjuster and ask whether biohazard remediation is covered and what the limit is.

items.q: Can I be there while you work?
items.a: You can, but most people find it better not to be. We can work from a key handover and send you photographs as we go.
Anything that can be safely recovered and cleaned, we return to you. Tell us at the assessment what matters to you, because once material is disposed of as regulated waste it cannot be retrieved.

items.q: Do you clean up fingerprint powder and evidence residue?
items.a: Yes. Investigators leave it behind and it is part of the job, not an extra.

items.q: Can the property be sold afterwards?
items.a: Yes. Our written clearance documents the property as remediated, which is what buyers and their lenders want to see. Disclosure rules are a question for your solicitor or estate agent, not for us.

items.q: How fast can you get here?
items.a: Our phone is answered 24 hours. On site, usually within two hours of the scene being released, anywhere in Montgomery County.
We do not publish ranges. We assess at no charge and give you a written price before any work starts, and we tell you at that visit what your insurer is likely to cover.

cta.heading: Call, and we will take it from there
cta.body: You do not need to explain anything on the phone. Give us the address and how to get in. Everything else we work out when we arrive.

form.heading: Request a discreet call back
form.body: We call you. No signage, no questions on the doorstep.
